references.text: The Lord commanded Moses to write down the events in a book, which shows Moses' role as the recorder of God's words and actions.
Moses wrote down all the Lord's words, confirming his practice of documenting God's revelation and Israel's history.
Moses wrote down the law and handed it over to the priests, showing his responsibility to preserve God's instructions in writing.
Moses wrote a song on that same day, further confirming his role as the author of holy texts at the Lord's command.
The travels of the Israelites were directed by the Lord's cloud, which explains the expression 'at the Lord's command' regarding their journeys.
A detailed description of how Israel's departures and encampments occurred at the Lord's command through the cloud over the tabernacle.
The people set out for the first time at the Lord's command through Moses, which connects directly to the journeys mentioned in Numbers 33.
